title: New outbreak of mpox in Anchorage prompts advisory from state health officials

analysis.time: Between 2023 and 2025, there were only two Alaska cases.
analysis.location_and_population: Up to now, travel had been implicated in the spread of mpox in Alaska.
analysis.event: It usually takes three to 17 days after infection for symptoms to emerge, Rollins said, and in the first phase, the symptoms are flu-like: "fever, chills, fatigue, headache, sore muscles, and even swollen lymph nodes." The lesions develop in the second phase, with bumps that are firm to the touch or sometimes tender, she said.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The JYNNEOS vaccine , approved by the Food and Drug Administration in 2019, guards against both clades of mpox, as well as smallpox, a disease that historically killed much of the world's population but is now considered to have been eradicated.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Investigation of cases so far has focused on household pets that appear to have encountered infected voles or other small mammals.

analysis.brief_en: A colorized electron micrograph image shows mpox virus particles, in red and yellow, found within infected cells, colored blue. The virus particles are in various stages of maturity, which accounts for differences in shape. The image also features virus factories, shown in brown, where viruses replicate, mature and assemble. (Image provided by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases/National Institutes of Health) A rare viral disease has emerged in an outbreak in Alaska's largest city that appears to be expanding, state health officials report. There are now four new cases in Anchorage of mpox , a viral disease formerly called monkeypox that is spread through close contact and can be fatal. None of the patients reported traveling outside the state in month-long period before becoming infected. It is the highest number of annual mpox cases in Alaska since 2022, when five cases were diagnosed in the state amid a global outbreak .

analysis.time: The study analyzed data from 2024 and 2025, with case counts returning to background levels by the end of December 2025. The article was published on November 8, 2026.

analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: A total of 5,322 reported MPXV infections were analyzed, with 2,803 cases in 2024 and 2,519 in 2025. analysis.location_and_population: Up to now, travel had been implicated in the spread of mpox in Alaska.
analysis.event: It usually takes three to 17 days after infection for symptoms to emerge, Rollins said, and in the first phase, the symptoms are flu-like: “fever, chills, fatigue, headache, sore muscles, and even swollen lymph nodes.” The lesions develop in the second phase, with bumps that are firm to the touch or sometimes tender, she said.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The JYNNEOS vaccine , approved by the Food and Drug Administration in 2019, guards against both clades of mpox, as well as smallpox, a disease that historically killed much of the world’s population but is now considered to have been eradicated.

analysis.brief_en: FILE - This colorized electron microscope image provided by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases in 2024 shows mpox virus particles, green, found within infected cultured cells, blue. The virus particles are in various stages of maturity, which accounts for differences in shape. analysis.time: The scoping review was conducted with final database searches completed on 19 September 2025, and the review was published on 8 November 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The review focused on global healthcare settings, with a noted geographic skew towards high-income countries and limited representation from Africa and low- and middle-income nations. The affected populations were pregnant women and children.
analysis.event: A scoping review identified critical data gaps regarding mpox vaccine effectiveness and implementation in pregnant women and children, as these groups were underrepresented in the literature and lacked specific safety and efficacy data.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The review highlighted that vaccine effectiveness estimates were derived almost entirely from adult populations, with no specific data for pregnant women or children. It also noted implementation barriers such as supply limitations, cold-chain constraints, and vaccine hesitancy, particularly during pregnancy.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The review documented key facilitators for vaccination programs, including international coordination, targeted surveillance, and integration into maternal and child health services. analysis.brief_en: A scoping review published on 8 November 2026 by Bioengineer.org identified critical data gaps in mpox vaccine effectiveness and implementation for pregnant women and children. The review, which completed its final database searches on 19 September 2025, found that vaccine effectiveness estimates were largely based on adult populations, with no specific data for these vulnerable groups. It noted significant implementation barriers, including supply limitations, cold-chain and logistical constraints, and vaccine hesitancy driven by safety concerns, especially during pregnancy. The review also highlighted the absence of randomised controlled clinical trials in pregnant women and children, as well as limited geographic representation from low- and middle-income countries. Despite these challenges, the authors identified key facilitators such as international coordination, targeted surveillance, and integration of immunisation into routine maternal and child health services. The review underscores the urgent need for prospective studies in these populations, equitable vaccine access, and tailored risk communication to address hesitancy.

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-11-04. Event date: Jan 1 to Oct 31, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Affected population: individuals with mpox symptoms, including rashes, blisters, or sores.
analysis.event: Thailand reported 470 mpox cases and 3 deaths between Jan 1 and Oct 31, 2026. The Department of Disease Control urged people with suspicious symptoms to seek medical help quickly.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 470 confirmed mpox cases and 3 deaths reported in Thailand. Most patients recover with supportive care, but pregnant women, young children, and people with weak immunity face higher risk. PCR testing is required for confirmation, as symptoms can resemble herpes or chickenpox.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Thailand’s Department of Disease Control is conducting surveillance, emphasizing early diagnosis, isolation, and prevention measures. They have issued guidelines on avoiding close contact, sharing items, and sexual activity with suspected cases. The department also highlighted the importance of privacy and reducing stigma to encourage early medical consultation.

analysis.brief_en: Thailand has reported 470 cases of mpox and three deaths between January 1 and October 31, 2026, according to the Department of Disease Control. The outbreak has prompted public health officials to urge individuals experiencing rashes, blisters, or sores to seek medical attention promptly. Mpox symptoms can resemble those of herpes or chickenpox, necessitating PCR testing for confirmation. Most patients recover with supportive care, but vulnerable groups such as pregnant women, young children, and immunocompromised individuals are at higher risk. The department has advised avoiding close contact, sharing personal items, and sexual activity with suspected cases to prevent transmission. They also emphasized the importance of privacy and reducing stigma to encourage timely medical consultation. The outbreak is being monitored under Thailand’s Communicable Diseases Act 2015, and officials are focusing on early diagnosis, isolation, and public awareness to curb further spread.
